_readme: The subject of a picture: the one thing raised off the surface, with a
shadow under it, while the picture is being PAINTED. Keyed by puzzle id,
value is the cell ids of its silhouette. Untagged pictures stay flat.
Separate from animations.json on purpose. That tag says what is alive in
the PHOTO — water that ripples, a lamp that glows — and it is chosen for
motion, not for mass. The two are rarely the same thing: on Humpback
Whale the ripple sits on the pectoral fin, so deriving the lift from it
raised a fin off a flat whale.
Pick an OBJECT, whole: a boat, a bowl, a tree, the whole animal. Not a
region (water, sky, an aurora), not a part of one. Pictures whose subject
is a texture rather than a thing are better left out than forced — half
the shipped pictures below have no entry for exactly that reason.
Past LIFT_MAX_AREA of the picture nothing is raised, because a lift needs
background to move against. See drawLift() in src/render.js.
Same rules as animations.json: this file is the source of truth, not the
puzzle JSON, which mapify.mjs rewrites from scratch on every bake.
writePuzzle() and apply-animations.mjs inject the `lift` field from here.
Use `node tools/tag-animation.mjs <id> --lift --cells 1,2,3` to set one.
region (water, sky). When the subject IS the lights or the clouds — an
aurora, a nebula — tag them whole; a scattered set (three koi, a bed of
anemones) rises as one and reads fine.
